_README: CURATED INPUT to scripts/otr_dropdown_matrix.py -- the ONLY hand-maintained half of the dropdown matrix. Everything else (which machines offer an engine, how its weights arrive, how big they are) is derived from the registries and the fetch manifests and must never be typed here. memory verdicts: proven (a PUBLISHED EPISODE used it) | measured (it ran on that hardware in a lab test, but no episode has used it) | fits (arithmetic only) | oom | no | unknown. The proven/measured split is not pedantry: it is the go-forward test plan, because 'measured' is exactly the list of things still to close. A 'proven' on a machine whose profile refuses the engine is a build failure, not a row. The `writers` block is the same shape as `engines` but keyed on HF repo id; writer machine-fit is DERIVED from _otr_model_catalog.fit_tags_for, so only receipts are curated here. NVIDIA verdicts were harvested from real receipts in docs/4060_DRILL_LOG.md, docs/ship-audit-2026-09-01/ and apple/MACHINE_MATRIX.md on 2026-09-09; AMD has ONE receipt as of 2026-09-14: an outside tester ran otr_amd_still end to end on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB, RDNA4/gfx1201) under Ubuntu 24.04 + ROCm 7.2 + PyTorch 2.9.1, pack commit 0b38424, clean pass. Only the engines that run ATTESTS in their own artifacts are marked proven here -- viz_mxc_cpu and still_motion from qa_report.json's per-beat engine_ids, plus kokoro and z_image_turbo named in their CHANGES.md. Their music line reads 'musicgen/stable-audio' and is ambiguous, so no music engine is marked. Everything else on AMD stays '?': RDNA3, Windows, the 8 GB profile and every lane past the still tier are untested.
_nvidia_provenance: The nv8 and nv16 verdicts came from a 46-agent audit of all 61 engines on 2026-09-09 (8 GB Ada / 16 GB Blackwell), each grounded in the registries and adapters, with 42 load-bearing verdicts adversarially re-checked and 7 overturned. Unlike the Mac column these are mostly REASONED, not run: 'proven' still means a receipt in apple/MACHINE_MATRIX.md and nothing else.

animatediff15_lightning_video.note: TWO published Mac episodes now: lightning_mac_proof_2 (2026-09-09, 23 beats, 02:32:34) and lightning_mac_proof_3 (2026-09-09, 8 clips, 01:17:46, RESULT SUCCESS). The second was rendered specifically to prove the scoped-refusal change to _beat_hold on a live episode -- it had unit tests and a measured ceiling behind it but no render, because the render that would have proven it rebooted the host (PBUG-20260909-02). Rendered clean with nothing else competing for RAM, it published and the machine survived.

bark.note: MEASURED END TO END ON THIS M4, 2026-09-09, and the verdict moved from 'measured' to OOM on the numbers. It produces good audio -- 11.5 s of speech, finite, spectral flatness 0.031 -- but: (1) 11.7x SLOWER THAN REALTIME (134.6 s for 11.5 s), so an episode's minutes of dialogue is hours in the voice stage alone; (2) generation drove the process to an 18.0 GB phys_footprint on a 16 GB machine, which is swap. The cause is not the weights: LIVE tensors never left 4.18 GB. The MPS caching allocator's RESERVED pool grew 5.10 -> 16.63 GB across the autoregressive loop and never gave it back -- after a full teardown, with ZERO live tensors, 10.85 GB stayed reserved and a second explicit torch.mps.empty_cache() returned none of it. kokoro is why all seven published episodes used kokoro.

flux3_klein.note: Proven on both NVIDIA cards by published episodes, read from the fk3i filename tag. 8 GB: it is the still engine of every otr_8gb_* graph, and the RTX 4060 Laptop published 39 episodes with it, among them the 2026-10-23 regression round's otr_8gb_still leg, marginalia_inversion_20261023_092210 (617 s for an 81.7 s episode, planning/regression/ROUNDS.md). 16 GB: the RTX 5080 Laptop holds 57 published fk3i episodes, among them white_elephant_zh_20261022_034407. On the 4060 a still paints in about 14 s (16 steps at about 1 s/it, the sampler bars in that box's server log).

flux3_klein_ref.note: The same model files as flux3_klein, with every character still painted from that character's portrait or the person's own photo. 16 GB: the RTX 5080 Laptop has published 14 My Story episodes with it (fk3r tag), among them sphere_visitation_20261022_110406 on the ltx25_foley_16gb lane (n16f tag); the filename does not name the graph. 8 GB: proven 2026-10-23 on the RTX 4060 Laptop -- otr_8gb_still with its character stills switched to flux3_klein_ref, the operator's GUSTO My Story cast of four, 1 act, published side_b_20261023_173305 (fk3r): 16 character stills painted from the four characters' portraits (otr_ref_* references in that box's server log), peak VRAM 7,495 MiB of 8,188, no OOM, 3,335 s for a 113.0 s episode (29.5 s/s). No photos were given, so the portraits came from the cast text.

kokoro.note: CPU proven 2026-09-13 on the same otr_cpu_low leg -- Kokoro ran at 0.12x realtime on the CPU, which is about eight seconds of a 34.5 minute run.

ltx25_video.note: Same mix4x8 DiT and w4a8 encoder as ltx25_foley_16gb. MEASURED, not proven: that weight rendered a 97-frame clip on an RTX 5080 Laptop (205.3 s) and on an RTX 4060 Laptop (707.0 s), but no episode has published on this silent lane with it.

moss_image.note: Both NVIDIA cells proven 2026-10-23 on published episodes. 16 GB: the 5080 regression round's otr_16gb_still leg, final_duet_20261023_094104 (msim). 8 GB: otr_8gb_still with its three still engines switched to moss_image on the RTX 4060 Laptop, 1 act, afterlife_echoes_20261023_164258 (msim) -- the pack auto-downloaded all three files there first (SFT int8 ConvRot model, w4a8 GPTQ encoder, small VAE) with byte-verified sizes, peak VRAM 7,370 MiB of 8,188, no OOM. On the 4060 a MOSS still paints in about 69 s (25 steps at 2.75 s/it) against 14 s for flux3_klein (16 steps), both read from the sampler bars in that box's server log, and the leg ran 2,747 s for a 96.4 s episode (28.5 s/s, about 5 min of it the first-run download) against 617 s for 81.7 s (7.6 s/s) with flux3_klein the same day.

minimax_h3_video.note: nv8 oom is MEASURED, not reasoned, since 2026-09-28: otr_8gb_still with this lane in all three video roles, one act, on the 8 GB RTX 4060 (fresh 2.3.10 portable). Three beats rendered -- 145 frames, 612 frames over two chained segments, 139 frames -- at about 34 s per sampler step on a 141-frame clip and 95 s per step on a 260-frame one; the nvfp4 text encoder ran emulated on Ada. Beat 4 then died OUT OF MEMORY loading the text encoder, 2:54:27 in, with CUDA reporting 0 bytes free while PyTorch held only 213 MiB -- memory that was not handed back between beats rather than a model too big to load. No episode published.

musicgen.note: Re-measured end to end on this M4 2026-09-09 through the real adapter (generate_clip, guidance_scale 3.0): 5.1 s of audio in 10.3 s on mps -- 2.1x realtime, and 1.7x FASTER than cpu (17.3 s). Structured audio on both devices. Memory ratchets hard but recovers completely: live tensors stay at 2.20 GB while the MPS reserved pool grows to 15.88 GB (7.1x the weights), then returns to 0.05 GB on empty_cache -- unlike bark, which leaves 10.85 GB stranded. Still MEASURED not PROVEN: no published episode has used it, all seven used stable_audio_3, and its CC-BY-NC licence is why it is not a default candidate. NO QUALITY CLAIM IS MADE HERE: spectral flatness in this repo is a noise detector (~0.43 = noise), not a quality score, and readings vary with prompt and seed -- ours read below the noise floor on both devices and that is all it establishes. CPU proven 2026-09-13: otr_cpu_low published a one-act episode with ComfyUI in --cpu mode in 34.5 minutes, and that graph scores with musicgen.

razzle_ltx_8gb.note: Local razzle sibling of ltx_8gb (2026-09-17). Same 0.9.8 weights and 512x288 canvas; only the raised motion clause differs. Verdict is fits, not proven -- no published episode on this id yet.

spandrel_esrgan.note: SUSTAINED-LOAD MEASURED on this M4 2026-09-09, which was the largest untested Mac gap: none of the seven published episodes ran the upscale stage at all (every one used upscale_engine=off) and the only Metal receipt covered 2 frames. Driven 96 frames at production canvas (512x288 -> 1024x576) through the engine's own load -> upscale_frames path: reserved memory DEAD FLAT at 1.13 GB from frame 24 to 96, footprint flat at 1.54 GB, chunk time flat at 4.17-4.19 s (no thermal drift), and 0.07 GB after empty_cache. 0.53 s/frame projects to ~24 min for a 2,736-frame episode. IT DOES NOT RATCHET, unlike bark and musicgen -- a fixed-shape convolutional forward has no growing state, so the Metal allocator behaviour that costs those two is absent here. Still not `proven`: no published episode has run it, so wall-clock inside a real OTR_SilentComposite pass is projected, not observed.

rtx_vsr.note: NVIDIA RTX Video Super Resolution through NVIDIA's nvidia-vfx wheel (proprietary, ~540 MB, never a requirements.txt line; you install it into ComfyUI's Python yourself with pip, since the Comfy Registry forbids a node pack installing packages at run time; NVIDIA cards only). MEASURED on the RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GB 2026-10-14 on 48 real 1472x832 OTR frames: 11-14 ms a frame straight to 1920x1080 (Real-ESRGAN x2 fp16 then fit: 1,846 ms), about 2.5-3.0 GB device-wide during the run, including the ~1.5 GB desktop baseline (torch peak ~0.97 GB at x2). First published with it on the RTX 4060 on 2026-10-16: AnimateDiff episodes upscaled clip by clip. Where it cannot run (no nvidia-vfx, AMD, Mac, a GTX card) the composite falls back to off with a warning.

Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B.note: The shipped default, and the ONLY writer with a receipt on either machine. All SEVEN episodes published on the M4 used it (ledger creative_writing_model, filename q354b), and it carried a complete episode on a physical 8 GB RTX 4060 at 2.99 GiB resident / 14.47 tok/s under NF4. On Metal there is no NF4 -- bitsandbytes is excluded on darwin -- so the same row loads full bf16 at ~14 GB, which fits a 16 GB machine with no margin for anything else. It rebooted this host once, at the writer-to-video handover, with a test suite competing for RAM.

google/gemma-4-12b-it.note: nv8 WAS 'proven' and is corrected to 'measured' on 2026-09-12. This file's own rule is that proven means a PUBLISHED EPISODE used it, and no episode has. The 4060 loads this row standalone -- 48/48 GPU layers, 7,751 MiB -- and then fails in the pipeline: 27 of 27 attempts at Step 15, and CR-20260912-06 now refuses it even earlier, at the fit gate, with 'estimated 11.9 GB peak resident vs 6.8 GB ceiling'. The drill log asks in as many words that it not be reported as qualified. nv16 goes the other way on a real receipt: the_cocks_trumpet_20260912_210724.

google/gemma-4-E2B-it.note: LOOKS smaller than Qwen3.5-4B and MEASURES LARGER on Metal: ~10 GB at bf16 against Qwen's ~9, like for like (apple/MAC_LESSONS_LEARNED.md, 'Levers that do NOT work'). Its small catalog figure is an NF4 number and there is no Metal NF4 kernel, so no Mac ever gets it.

google/gemma-4-E4B-it.note: The 8 GB 'measured' is a run, not a fit: on the RTX 4060 8 GB it loads only through the loader's CPU offload, at 0.5 tok/s at its first heartbeat (2026-09-06, PBUG-20260906-06); the loader's planner needs roughly 12 GiB of free RAM for that offload. Loading it all on the GPU as NF4 ran out of memory there at 7.19 GiB (2026-10-14), which is why it carries no nv8 tag.
